overview.title: Baja Cape Loop
overview.subtitle: 9.5 riding days + 1 rest day · clockwise · January
overview.direction: Clockwise: San José del Cabo → Todos Santos → La Paz → East Cape → Cabo Pulmo → San José del Cabo
overview.season: January — peak season. Highs ~70s°F / lows ~50s°F; cold nights at elevation.
overview.logistics: Riders are NOT flying in. Dropped off at the San José del Cabo start; finish near Cabo (Ventanas basecamp) where bike boxes / gear are staged. Day 1 is a full riding day — there is no fly-in half day and no Cabo-lodging finish day.
overview.tubeless: Tubeless tires are MANDATORY (cactus spines). Riders run 27.5×2.8 plus, which is in-spec.
overview.source_note: Daily structure from Sarah Swallow's 11-day itinerary, adjusted for drop-off/basecamp logistics. Distances/dry-carry gaps from the Resupply Sheet. Distances are planning estimates derived from RWGPS section totals.

days.title: San José del Cabo → Sierra de la Laguna
highlights: Full riding day from the drop-off — no fly-in half day.
Climb Las Naranjas road, one of the only roads through the Sierra de la Laguna.
Low pass, descent, then a higher second pass with Pacific Ocean views.
days.camp: Wild camp near the pass / upper Las Naranjas road.
days.water_note: Top off fully in San José del Cabo — no services on the climb.

days.title: Descend to Todos Santos
highlights: Long, fun descent down the west side of the mountains.
Undulating run into Todos Santos, a snowbird favorite with real community.
Full resupply + internet before the longest dry carry of the loop.
days.water_note: Resupply town. Fill EVERY bottle here for tomorrow's dry carry.

shortcut.name: Playa Los Cerritos detour
shortcut.detail: 16 mi round-trip to the best surf beach on the cape (board rentals, lessons, beach camping). Junction is at the Turn for Los Cerritos.

days.title: Todos Santos → Sierra crossing (dry carry)
days.to: Camp near Valle Perdido / El Rosario
highlights: Dusty farm roads (close all cattle gates) climbing into the national park edge.
Sandy tracks even while climbing; old road bed rides like singletrack.
Drainage with possible water and great campsites before the pass.
days.camp: Wild camp in a Sierra drainage (seasonal water) near El Rosario.
days.water_note: DRY CARRY — Todos Santos → El Rosario, 33.7 mi / 54 km. The loop's longest carry; no reliable water on the climb. First reliable water at El Rosario.

days.title: El Triunfo → La Paz
highlights: 1.5 mi detour to El Triunfo — restored mining town, stores + two sit-down eateries.
Scenic Los Divisaderos road, slowly climbing to its high point.
Finish with ~15 miles of downhill into colorful La Paz.
days.camp: La Paz — hotel / hostel. FWMCRB$ Bus Airport.
days.water_note: Resupply at El Triunfo (1.5 mi off route) and Los Divisaderos. Easy water into La Paz.

days.title: Rest day — La Paz
highlights: Whale shark tours from the malecón (January is prime season).
Full resupply, ATMs, laundry, bike shop, real coffee + tacos.
Drivetrain check + sealant top-off before the East Cape half.
days.water_note: Rest + resupply hub. Stage water for the climb out of town tomorrow.

days.title: La Paz → San Juan de los Planes (climb out)
highlights: Paved climb out of La Paz to ~2000′, then a gorgeous dirt road down to Los Divisaderos.
Climb the ridge for spectacular views of San Juan de los Planes and the Sea of Cortez.
Sandy tracks back to pavement into San Juan de los Planes.
days.camp: San Juan de los Planes (FWR) or nearby beach.
days.water_note: DRY CARRY — La Paz → Los Divisaderos, 30.3 mi / 49 km, climbing out of La Paz. Carry near-full from town.

shortcut.name: La Paz → San Juan de los Planes shortcut
shortcut.detail: 30.5 mi paved alternate that skips the Los Divisaderos dirt climb. Faster and lower if anyone needs an easier day.

days.title: East Cape coast → La Ribera
highlights: Rough dirt over the ridge to the sea, then ~15 mi of the most scenic rocky coastal road on the Baja Divide.
Resupply options at El Cardonal; near-empty coast road east of San Juan de los Planes.
Los Barriles (largest East Cape resupply) then mostly flat to La Ribera.
days.camp: La Ribera (FWMR) — load up here for Cabo Pulmo.
days.water_note: Plenty of resupply (El Cardonal, Los Barriles, La Ribera). Fill fully at La Ribera for tomorrow.

days.title: La Ribera → Cabo Pulmo (short day)
highlights: Short day on purpose — Cabo Pulmo has the best snorkeling in Baja + favorite singletrack.
National marine park; reef just offshore.
Beach camp at Los Frailes / Cabo Pulmo.
days.camp: Cabo Pulmo / Los Frailes beach camp.
days.water_note: DRY CARRY — La Ribera → Cabo Pulmo, 20.1 mi / 32 km. Cabo Pulmo is limited (two restaurants, no store) — LOAD PAST IT at La Ribera.

days.title: Cabo Pulmo → Palo Escopeta (big climb)
highlights: South of Los Frailes, the climb away from the sea is sandy for the first ~4 mi / 800′.
Firmer road above 800′, climbing past several steep drainages.
Big views of Mt. Trinidad and the Sierra de la Laguna at the top.
days.camp: Wild camp near Palo Escopeta (tiny store, limited hours).
days.water_note: DRY CARRY — Cabo Pulmo → Palo Escopeta, 26.2 mi / 42 km. Big climb day; only a tiny stop at the end. Carry full from Cabo Pulmo (top off at La Ribera the day before).

days.title: Palo Escopeta → finish near Cabo
days.to: San José del Cabo → Ventanas basecamp
highlights: Long descent back to civilization at the north end of San José del Cabo.
Loop closes near the airport / Santa Anita.
Transfer to the Ventanas basecamp to break down bikes and pack boxes.
days.camp: Ventanas basecamp (staging for bike boxes / gear).
days.water_note: Short descent day. Water in Palo Escopeta and San José del Cabo.
